candidate_relations.reason: The clinical record shows granulomatous/histiocytic infiltrate with atypical lymphocytes, systemic involvement (bone marrow clonal T-cells, restrictive lung disease, arthritis), CD3-negative/CD8-positive flow cytometry phenotype, and steroid-dependent course — features more consistent with granulomatous CTCL than classic mycosis fungoides. While both are CD8+ CTCL subtypes, mycosis fungoides has a distinct epidermotropic pattern and clinical staging that conflicts with the granulomatous subtype specified in the reference. The granulomatous qualifier is a required component of the reference diagnosis that C001 omits and implicitly contradicts by asserting MF.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Mycosis fungoides is a specific subtype of cutaneous T-cell lymphoma with distinct clinicopathologic features; the reference specifies granulomatous CTCL with CD8+ phenotype, which is a separate entity from classic MF

case_quality_flags: Bone marrow involvement and systemic features (arthritis, restrictive lung disease) suggest advanced/systemic granulomatous CTCL rather than classic MF
CD3-negative but CD5/CD8-positive flow cytometry phenotype is atypical and supports a non-MF granulomatous CTCL diagnosis
